<p dir="auto">When your agent run costs more than you expected, this tells you which sub-agent spent it, and how much you paid to resend the same context.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">What it does</h2><a id="user-content-what-it-does" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: What it does" href="#what-it-does"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Per-sub-agent totals — input and output tokens grouped by agent, then by step.</li>
<li>Cost ranking — every step in the run, sorted by dollar cost, highest first.</li>
<li>Repeated-context detection — flags context blocks sent more than once across steps, with repeat count, estimated wasted tokens, which detection mechanism found it, and the step names and locations where it occurred. Locations are a span id when the trace carries one, otherwise a line number — in practice, none of the three bundled fixtures (<code>sample.jsonl</code>, <code>sample-broken.jsonl</code>, <code>real-trace.jsonl</code>) has a span id on any span that's part of a repeated block, so line numbers are what you'll actually see today.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Install</h2><a id="user-content-install" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Install" href="#install"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Requires Python 3.10+ (the code uses <code>str | None</code> union syntax). No dependencies — standard library only.
<code>tools/</code> has its own dependencies (see <code>tools/README.md</code>) for reproducing a real trace; the tool itself still has none.</p>

<p dir="auto">The tool reads OpenInference spans as JSONL, one span per line, so it should
work against anything that exports that format — Phoenix, Langfuse, or plain
OpenTelemetry instrumented with OpenInference semantic conventions. In
practice it has been tested against the bundled <code>sample.jsonl</code> /
<code>sample-broken.jsonl</code> fixtures and exactly one real trace: a three-node
linear LangGraph run (research → write → review). Phoenix, Langfuse,
CrewAI, and AutoGen exports have not been run through it.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Pricing</h2><a id="user-content-pricing" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Pricing" href="#pricing"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Repeated-context detection</h2><a id="user-content-repeated-context-detection" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Repeated-context detection" href="#repeated-context-detection"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Two independent signals, run over every <code>llm.input_messages.*.message.content</code>
value:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>normalized-exact</strong> — message content is normalized (whitespace runs
collapsed to a single space, ends stripped; case and punctuation are left
alone since both change what a prompt means) and hashed. Two occurrences
land in the same group if they hash the same, even if a stray space or
newline makes them byte-different. This catches the case a tiny
formatting edit used to hide a recurring block entirely.</li>
<li><strong>prefix</strong> — the existing v0.1 detector: a long shared <em>leading</em>
substring (200+ characters), for a stable header (e.g. a system prompt)
followed by different per-step content.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Each row in the repeat table is labeled with whichever mechanism found it,
or <code>both</code> if the exact same set of steps was found by each independently.</p>

<p dir="auto">SOURCE distinguishes a span's own reported cost (<code>reported</code>) from a price computed from <code>prices.json</code> (<code>computed</code>). A step whose model has no entry in <code>prices.json</code>, or that has no <code>llm.model_name</code> at all, shows <code>n/a</code> for cost — same as if <code>prices.json</code> itself were missing or unreadable.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">What it does not do</h2><a id="user-content-what-it-does-not-do" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: What it does not do" href="#what-it-does-not-do"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>No live dashboard. No server, no web UI, no hosted anything. One command, text output.</li>
<li>No trends over time. It explains a single run, not many runs across days.</li>
<li>No optimization suggestions. It shows a context block was resent nine times. It does not tell you how to fix it.</li>
<li>No instrumentation. It does not wrap your LLM calls or collect traces. You bring a log; it reads it.</li>
<li>Prices for two models ship in <code>prices.json</code>. Adding more is a JSON edit, not a code change, but nothing beyond those two is bundled.</li>
<li>OpenInference spans only, with one LangGraph-specific fallback: if a span
has no <code>agent.name</code> or <code>graph.node.name</code>, the tool looks for a
<code>langgraph_node</code> key inside the OpenInference <code>metadata</code> attribute. No
other framework-specific log formats.</li>
</ul>
